sections.h2: Who sends a LaRue County property tax bill, and who answers questions about it?
sections.html:
Almost every LaRue County tax office sits inside the courthouse complex on West High Street in Hodgenville, and Hodgenville homeowners get a second bill from City Hall. The sheriff sends and collects the county bill, the PVA sets the value, the clerk takes in bills left unpaid, and the county attorney works on delinquent ones.

  • Sheriff's Office. 209 West High Street, Suite 6; weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.; (270) 358-3120.
  • Property valuation administrator. Value, exemptions and appeal conferences; (270) 358-4202.
  • County clerk. Suite 3 at the same address; weekdays until 4:30 p.m.; (270) 358-3544.
  • County attorney. Suite 8; (270) 358-9223.
  • Hodgenville City Hall. 200 S. Lincoln Blvd.; (270) 358-3832 for the city bill.

Call the PVA before paying when a figure looks off. The sheriff collects whatever amount the bill shows and has no say over value.

sections.h2: What is LaRue County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
LaRue County is rural, 264 square miles of low rolling hills in central Kentucky outside the Bluegrass. Hodgenville, the seat, had 3,235 people in 2020 and is where Abraham Lincoln was born. Hardin County gave up its southeastern corner to create LaRue on March 4, 1843, and the county belongs to the Elizabethtown-Fort Knox metro area. Upton, mostly in Hardin County, is the only other city. Buffalo and Magnolia are census-designated places. Kentucky Route 61 runs the 12 miles northwest to Elizabethtown, and U.S. 31E passes through the middle of Hodgenville toward Bardstown and Glasgow.

One school district, LaRue County Schools, serves the whole county, with its campuses in Hodgenville. Lincoln Days fills downtown on the first full weekend of October. LaRue is also a dry county, which matters to anyone trying to sell a building for restaurant use.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about LaRue County housing?
sections.html:
The county grew from 14,867 residents in 2020 to an estimated 15,184 in July 2025, a gain of 2.1 percent. It holds 6,763 housing units. Census survey results for 2020 through 2024 set it apart from the mountain counties to the east:

  • Owners value a typical home they live in at $183,500.
  • About four in five of the 5,996 households own their homes.
  • A typical monthly rent is $860.
  • A typical household takes in $67,067 a year, and 14.1 percent of residents live below the poverty line.
  • Workers average 28.2 minutes to get to a job.
  • 59 building permits were issued in 2025.

Higher values mean larger tax bills for the same rate, and they make a clean payoff worth the effort before listing.

sections.h2: When do LaRue County bills come due?
sections.html:
The county attorney's office says bills usually go out in October with a December 31 due date, and the sheriff accepts payment from November 1 to April 15. Bills for the 2026 year were mailed on October 30, 2026, and the city bills were mailed around the same time. The schedule printed for them follows.

Payment steps for 2026 LaRue County bills (source: local newspaper notice of the sheriff's and city's schedule)
Paid betweenAmount owed
November 1 and 30, 2026Face amount less a 2% discount
December 1 and 31, 2026Face amount
January 1 and 31, 2027Face amount plus a 5% penalty
After February 1, 2027Face amount plus a 10% penalty, and a possible 11% sheriff's fee on county bills

Paying online by card adds a 2.5 percent fee. A drop box in the courthouse foyer is open around the clock. By mail, enclose the bill or its number, plus a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt. These steps are reset each year, so check the bill itself.

sections.h2: Is there a separate Hodgenville city tax bill?
sections.html:
Yes. A parcel inside the city gets a county bill from the sheriff and a city bill from City Hall, and the two are paid in different places. City payments go to City Hall, the city website or the city drop box, and the same November 30 cutoff earns the 2 percent discount. A parcel outside the city limits gets only the county bill.

When you buy or sell in Hodgenville, ask the closing agent to confirm that both bills are paid or prorated. The sheriff's page also carries a fire dues waiver form, and the online portal cannot remove fire dues, so an owner seeking a waiver files it at the sheriff's office.

sections.h2: What if my LaRue County assessment is too high?
sections.html:
Ask the PVA, at (270) 358-4202, for a conference. Kentucky requires one before any appeal. Value is set as of January 1, and the tax roll opens for inspection in early May. After that conference the appeal goes to the county clerk right after the inspection period ends, and a board of local property owners hears it within weeks.

The board denies a case that arrives without evidence, so assemble recent sales of similar homes, an appraisal, repair bids or insurance values. The county attorney's office helps the PVA with assessment appeals, according to its page on the county site.

sections.h2: What happens to an unpaid LaRue County bill?
sections.html:
On April 15 the bill goes to the clerk and turns into a certificate of delinquency, a lien on the real estate under KRS 134.122. Whoever owned the property on January 1 of that tax year also owes the bill personally. Penalties and fees are added, and interest at 12 percent a year under KRS 134.125 makes the total rise every month.

  • The county attorney mails two notices before any certificate is sold.
  • After 90 days, KRS 134.452 lets outside buyers purchase it by paying the amount due.
  • The first batch of certificates is usually offered at a tax bill sale in August.
  • An unsold certificate is paid at the clerk's office, Suite 3, 209 W. High Street.
  • A certificate that has been sold must be paid to the buyer.

A certificate cannot be sold while a payment agreement with the county attorney is in place or while the parcel is tied up in foreclosure or bankruptcy litigation that includes that office. The county attorney arranges payment plans on unsold certificates at (270) 358-9223.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the homestead exemption in LaRue County?
sections.html:
The state set the deduction at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Owners aged 65 or older, or totally disabled under a retirement system, can use it on a home they own and live in on January 1. Apply to the PVA, (270) 358-4202, by the end of December.

The deduction lowers assessed value, so the savings depend on the combined county, school, city and district rates on your parcel. Heirs who take over a house should ask the PVA what changes once the title moves.

sections.h2: How are LaRue County taxes handled when a house sells?
sections.html:
The January 1 owner is the person on that year's bill, so a spring closing still leaves the seller named. The settlement statement usually divides the year, and the closing agent pays the sheriff. The deed must carry an in-care-of address for the transfer-year bill under KRS 382.135(1)(d), which means giving the buyer's mailing address.

Before listing a LaRue County house with back taxes, collect two numbers: the current-year amount from the sheriff and any delinquent certificate balance from the clerk. Houses that were inherited, behind on payments or too worn for a standard listing can often close faster in a direct cash sale, and the payoffs come out of that one closing as long as they were requested ahead of time.

faqs.q: Who takes LaRue County property tax payments?
faqs.a: The sheriff's office at 209 West High Street, Suite 6, by mail, online or in the courthouse drop box. Hodgenville city bills go to City Hall at 200 S. Lincoln Blvd.

faqs.q: Until when did the 2026 LaRue County discount last?
faqs.a: Payments made through November 30, 2026 earned a 2% discount. December 1 through 31 required the face amount, January 2027 added 5%, and after that the penalty is 10%.

faqs.q: How fast does a late LaRue County bill grow?
faqs.a: After April 15 it becomes a certificate of delinquency that earns 12 percent interest a year, plus penalties and fees. The county attorney can discuss a plan if the certificate is unsold.

faqs.q: Where do I sign up for the LaRue County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: At the PVA, (270) 358-4202, before December 31. Applicants must be 65 or older, or totally disabled under a retirement system, and live in the home they own on January 1.

faqs.q: May I sell a LaRue County house while taxes are overdue?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays on the parcel, so the payoff is deducted at closing. Get written amounts from the sheriff and the clerk before picking a date.
